title: Strings: Is Palindrome
oneLiner: Two pointers again, but comparing instead of swapping -- read from both ends toward the middle.
keyTakeaway: Strings are effectively character arrays, so array techniques (two pointers, sliding window) apply directly. The one catch: in C# and Python, strings are immutable (can't be changed after they're created) -- anything beyond read-only comparison needs a new string, not in-place mutation like an int[] gets.
explanation: First string problem, and it reuses a tool you already have: two pointers starting at opposite ends. Instead of swapping (like reversing an array), just compare -- if the characters at left and right ever disagree, it's not a palindrome; if the pointers meet or cross without a disagreement, it is. Watch out for two edge cases interview problems love to sneak in: an empty string (trivially a palindrome -- the loop should just never run) and case/spacing (this version assumes a clean lowercase string with no spaces; "real" palindrome-checking problems usually ask you to normalize first).
